intro.lead: BAYAN searches several scholarly libraries at once and brings the results into one place. Use a research area to find related work, read abstracts, choose the papers that matter, export them, identify candidate research gaps and develop 1–5 research proposals.
intro.note: The gap and proposal buttons prepare an evidence prompt for you to submit; BAYAN does not run the analysis automatically yet. Evidence is limited to titles, metadata and abstracts. Candidate gaps and novelty claims need checking against full texts and a wider literature search. Hover over any button for help.
intro.s1.body: Type your research area. Choose libraries, reference types, languages and years, then click Search.
intro.s1.head: Define your area.
intro.s2.body: Open an abstract with Show abstract, follow the source link, and tick the papers you want to keep.
intro.s2.head: Read and choose.
intro.s3.body: Download the ticked papers (or all results) as an Excel workbook or a CSV file.
intro.s3.head: Export.
intro.s4.body: Choose how many gaps you want (1–5) and click Find research gaps. Copy the evidence prompt into an AI assistant and submit it.
intro.s4.head: Find research gaps.
intro.s5.body: Paste the gap(s) you want to pursue, choose 1–5 proposals, and click Create proposals. Submit the new prompt the same way.
intro.s5.head: Develop proposals.
intro.title: From a research topic to a proposal

member.help: An email address alone gives no access to paid content. Here you can store your own publisher API keys (encrypted on the server, never shown again) and an institutional proxy link. No connector uses these keys yet, so saving a key does not change any search or download today. BAYAN never logs in for you, never fetches through your proxy and never stores a library password.

rel.title: How reliable is BAYAN for your field?
rel.lead: Test agents used BAYAN the way researchers in {areas} subfields would, for {from}–{to}: they searched their field, looked up known papers by title ({gold} verified papers in all) and exported BibTeX. Test run of {date}.
rel.none: No reliability test has been published yet.
rel.help: Score = 30 known papers found by title + 20 results in the field + 15 the field's own papers found + 10 no shortfall + 10 no errors + 10 correct metadata + 5 integrity (years, DOIs, BibTeX).
